title: Pharmaceutical Industry in Bangladesh: How Does It Work?
alt: Pharmaceutical industry in Bangladesh, how medicines reach you

p: Research, development, manufacturing, quality checks, regulation and distribution all work together.
slides.alt: The complete journey of a medicine in seven stages
slides.r: A tablet is the last step of a long journey.

p: Innovator, generic, API, biotech, CRO and CDMO organisations play different roles.
Their activities can overlap.
The API is the active ingredient.
Excipients and the dosage form turn it into the tablet or capsule you take.
GMP, QA, QC, regulatory affairs and pharmacovigilance each protect a different part of quality and safety.
slides.alt: GMP, quality assurance and quality control compared

p: BIDA’s profile says local manufacturers meet about 98% of domestic medicine demand.
It also says over 85% of API needs are imported.
slides.r: These profile figures carry no year.

title: When to Take a PPI: Before Meals, Common Mistakes
alt: When to take a PPI: before meals, with food or on an empty stomach

p: A proton pump inhibitor reduces stomach acid.
Omeprazole, lansoprazole and rabeprazole are examples.
Used for ulcers, heartburn and reflux (NHS).
The FDA label says rabeprazole tablets can be taken with or without food for most uses, with named exceptions.
Omeprazole advice varies by source and product.
slides.alt: When to take a PPI: timing and food

p: Swallow with water.
Do not chew or crush gastro-resistant tablets or capsules unless the label says so.
slides.alt: Swallow a PPI whole with water

p: Sources name warfarin, clopidogrel, digoxin and iron among medicines to mention to your pharmacist.
slides.alt: Medicines named in NHS, MedlinePlus and a UK rabeprazole leaflet
slides.r: Always tell your pharmacist what else you take.

p: Take a missed dose when you remember, unless the next is nearly due.
Never take two doses together.
Persistent or severe symptoms need a doctor.
slides.alt: When to see a doctor about PPI use

end.t: Follow your own label, and ask a pharmacist if you are unsure.
end.alt: Key takeaways for using a PPI safely

title: How to Take Iron Tablets Properly: Timing, Food & Interactions
alt: How to take iron tablets properly

p: The NHS says iron works best on an empty stomach: about 30 minutes before eating or 2 hours after a meal.
If it upsets your stomach, ask about taking it with food.
Vitamin C may help absorption.
Tea, coffee, eggs, dairy and calcium can reduce it.
slides.alt: What helps and reduces iron absorption

p: NIH names levothyroxine and levodopa as medicines iron can affect.
PPIs lower stomach acid and may reduce iron absorption.
Stomach upset, constipation, nausea and abdominal pain can happen.
Darker stools are a known effect.
slides.alt: Iron tablet side effects and missed dose
slides.r: Black or bloody stools or severe stomach pain need a doctor.

p: Keep iron tablets out of sight and reach of children.
Accidental overdose is dangerous.
slides.alt: Keep iron tablets away from children

end.t: Take it exactly as prescribed and do not stop early. Tell your pharmacist about your other medicines.
end.alt: How to take iron tablets properly

title: Iron Deficiency vs Anemia: Differences, Symptoms & Tests

p: Iron is the raw material.
Red blood cells, with hemoglobin, are the finished product.
Iron deficiency is the shortage.
Anemia is what the blood count shows.
Stores can run low before anemia appears.
slides.alt: Iron deficiency vs anemia: key differences

p: Per the NHS: tiredness, breathlessness, palpitations, paler skin and headaches.
slides.alt: Common symptoms of iron deficiency anemia

p: Heavy periods, bleeding and hookworm infection are among the causes.
Finding the cause matters as much as replacing iron.
A CBC and ferritin test come first.
Iron tablets are the usual treatment, often for around six months (NHS).
slides.alt: How iron deficiency anemia is diagnosed
slides.r: Do not take iron without a test.

end.h: KNOW WHEN TO SEE A DOCTOR
end.t: Ongoing tiredness, paler skin or breathlessness need a visit. Chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness need urgent help.

title: Heartburn vs Acid Reflux vs GERD: What's the Difference?
alt: Heartburn, acid reflux and GERD explained

p: Heartburn is the feeling.
Acid reflux is the event.
GERD is the repeating condition.
slides.alt: Esophagus, lower esophageal sphincter and stomach

p: The valve between the food pipe and stomach should close like a one-way door.
Reflux happens when it relaxes and acid rises.
Foods, drinks, meal timing, lifestyle factors and some medicines can trigger reflux.
Smaller, earlier meals.
Stay upright after eating.
Elevating the head of the bed can help.
slides.alt: Seven daily habits to reduce reflux

p: Amber signs mean see a doctor soon.
Red signs mean emergency help now.
slides.alt: Traffic-light guide to reflux warning signs

end.t: Medicines are a doctor’s decision. If symptoms keep coming back, get checked.

title: Expiry Date vs Manufacturing Date: Read Any Pack in 10 Seconds
alt: Expiry date vs manufacturing date on medicine

p: MFG: when it was made.
EXP: when it expires.
B.No.: which batch it is from.
slides.alt: Reading MFG, EXP and batch number

p: The manufacturing date tells you how old a pack is.
The expiry date is the last date the maker guarantees strength and safety, if stored as directed.
slides.alt: Manufacturing date on a blister strip

p: It identifies the production batch.
If there is a quality problem or recall, it helps trace the pack.
slides.r: Keep the pack or note the batch number when reporting a problem.

p: Short answer: no.
Strength can drop and you cannot tell by looking or smelling.
slides.alt: Valid, near expiry and expired medicines

p: Keep medicine in a closed cupboard or bedside table.
Avoid hot cars, steamy bathrooms and kitchen stoves.
slides.alt: Safe and unsafe places to store medicine

end.t: Read the dates, inspect the strip, check the pack for damage and read the leaflet.

title: Generic Name vs Brand Name: The Simple Guide
alt: Generic name vs brand name of a medicine

p: Generic name: the ingredient.
Then strength, dosage form and manufacturer.
slides.alt: Four parts of a medicine box

p: Finix 20 and Rabe-20 are different brands that both contain rabeprazole sodium 20 mg.
Generic name: the actual medicine.
Brand name: the product name.
Formulation: how it is made and released.
Tablet, capsule, MUPS, sprinkle capsule and more.
Same ingredient does not always mean same strength or form.
slides.alt: Five dosage forms of the same medicine

p: Tea leaves are the ingredient.
A green tea packet is the brand.
A tea bag is a different formulation.

end.t: Check the generic name, strength and form. Ask a pharmacist if you are unsure.

title: Drug vs Medicine: Meaning, Differences, Examples
alt: Drug vs medicine meaning and differences

p: The active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) that produces the effect in the body.
Example: rabeprazole.
A prepared product that contains a drug in a specific dose and form.
A tablet, capsule or syrup.
A drug is a chemical substance with biological action.
A medicine is a usable product to prevent, relieve or treat disease.
Rabeprazole is the drug.
Finix is a medicine containing it.
Finix MUPS is the same drug in a MUPS formulation.
Drug (API), formulation, manufacturing, then a quality check for safety, strength and quality.

end.t: A drug is the active substance. A medicine is a prepared, usable product.

title: Glucosamine and Alzheimer's: What the New Study Really Shows

p: Glucosamine has not been proven to cause Alzheimer’s.
A 2026 Nature Metabolism study found a warning signal.
Cells add sugar chains called glycans to proteins.
Alzheimer’s brains show too many glycans.
Human brain tissue, Alzheimer’s-model mice and hospital records from 2012 to 2024 for more than 50,000 people.
About 25% higher likelihood of progressing from MCI to dementia.
About 25% higher mortality in established dementia.
No mortality increase in the MCI group.
It does not prove cause and effect.
It is not a randomized trial.
It does not show the effect in people without memory problems.
slides.alt: What the study does not show

end.t: Discuss with your doctor before any change, and do not stop suddenly.
